meta.title: Pakistan Federal Budget
meta.note: All figures in Rs. billion. Top-level totals follow the official 'Budget at a Glance' (Table 1). Sub-category figures are drawn from the detailed tables (in Rs. million there, converted to billion) and may differ from a rounded parent total by small rounding amounts. Where a category has many line items, only the largest are broken out and the remainder is grouped as 'Other'.

nodes.label: FBR Tax Revenue
nodes.description: Taxes collected by the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) — the single largest source of federal money. Split into direct taxes (mainly income tax) and indirect taxes (sales tax, customs and federal excise).

nodes.label: Direct Taxes
nodes.description: Taxes levied directly on income and wealth. Overwhelmingly income tax, plus small levies (Capital Value Tax, Workers' Welfare Fund, Workers' Profit Participation Fund).

items.label: Growth over same period last year

nodes.label: Income Tax
nodes.description: Tax on the income of individuals and companies — the biggest single tax line in the federal budget.

nodes.label: Capital Value Tax
nodes.description: Tax on the capital value of certain assets.

nodes.label: Workers' Welfare Fund
nodes.description: Contributions to the Workers' Welfare Fund, collected with income tax.

nodes.label: Workers' Profit Participation Fund
nodes.description: Workers' share of company profits collected federally.

nodes.label: Indirect Taxes
nodes.description: Taxes on transactions and goods rather than income: general sales tax, customs duties on imports, and federal excise duty.

nodes.label: Sales Tax
nodes.description: General Sales Tax on goods — the largest indirect tax.

items.label: Growth over same period last year

nodes.label: Sales Tax (Goods)
nodes.description: GST on goods across the economy — imports and domestic supplies.

nodes.label: Sales Tax (Services, ICT)
nodes.description: Sales tax on services collected in Islamabad Capital Territory only (provinces tax services themselves).

nodes.label: Customs Duties
nodes.description: Duties levied on imported goods.

altBreakdowns.title: Gross collection by import category
altBreakdowns.note: Major revenue spinners, gross (Rs 1,721 bn) before refunds and rebates of Rs 70 bn — the node value is net collection. Export Development Surcharge was discontinued from Dec 2025.

items.label: Growth over same period last year

nodes.label: Federal Excise
nodes.description: Federal excise duty on selected manufactured goods and services.

items.label: Growth over same period last year

nodes.label: FED on Services
nodes.description: Federal excise duty on services (e.g. airline travel, telecom in ICT).

nodes.label: Cement
nodes.description: Excise duty on cement production.

nodes.label: Imported Goods
nodes.description: Excise duty collected on imported goods.

nodes.label: Cigarettes & Tobacco
nodes.description: Excise duty on cigarettes and tobacco products.

nodes.label: Beverages
nodes.description: Excise duty on beverages and beverage concentrate.

nodes.label: POL Products
nodes.description: Excise duty on petroleum, oil and lubricant products.

nodes.label: Natural Gas
nodes.description: Excise duty on natural gas (charged at well-head; not part of the divisible pool).

nodes.label: Other Items
nodes.description: Excise duty on all remaining items.

nodes.label: Non-Tax Revenue
nodes.description: Federal income that is not a tax — chiefly the State Bank of Pakistan's profit, the Petroleum Levy, dividends, and various fees and surcharges.

nodes.label: Levies & Fees
nodes.description: Mobile handset levy, ICT administration fees and airport fees.

nodes.label: Income from Property & Enterprises
nodes.description: Mark-up on loans to provinces and public-sector enterprises, dividends, and regulator surpluses (e.g. PTA spectrum licences).

nodes.label: Mark-up (PSEs & Others)
nodes.description: Interest received on federal loans to public-sector enterprises and others.

nodes.label: Dividends
nodes.description: Dividends on government shareholdings in state-owned and part-owned companies.

nodes.label: Mark-up (Provinces)
nodes.description: Interest received on federal loans extended to provincial governments.

nodes.label: PTA & Regulatory Authorities
nodes.description: PTA surplus and 4G/5G licence receipts (Rs 29 bn) plus surpluses/penalties of other regulatory authorities.

nodes.label: Civil Administration Receipts
nodes.description: Receipts from civil administration functions — dominated by the State Bank of Pakistan's surplus profit (Rs. 1,436 bn), plus defence, law-and-order and other administrative receipts.

nodes.label: State Bank Profit
nodes.description: Surplus profit of the State Bank of Pakistan transferred to the federal government. Sharply lower than last year’s Rs 2,400 bn as interest rates (and hence SBP earnings) fall.

nodes.label: Defence Receipts
nodes.description: Receipts of the defence establishment (services rendered, recoveries and miscellaneous defence income).

nodes.label: Other Civil Administration
nodes.description: General administration, law and order, community and social services receipts.

nodes.label: Miscellaneous Receipts
nodes.description: Largest components are the Petroleum Levy (Rs. 1,677 bn) and receipts from provinces under Article 164 (Rs. 1,035 bn), plus gas surcharge, royalties on oil and gas, passport fees and other levies.

nodes.label: Petroleum Levy
nodes.description: Levy charged on petroleum products at the pump — the largest non-tax revenue source, and unlike FBR taxes it is not shared with the provinces.

nodes.label: Provincial Receipts (Article 164)
nodes.description: Grants/receipts from provinces under Article 164 of the Constitution — a new entry for FY2026-27 with no counterpart in the 2025-26 budget.

nodes.label: Oil & Gas Royalties
nodes.description: Royalty on crude oil (Rs 45.5 bn) and natural gas (Rs 95 bn) paid by exploration companies.

nodes.label: Passport & Citizenship Fees
nodes.description: Citizenship, naturalization and passport fees.

nodes.label: Gas Development Surcharge
nodes.description: Natural Gas Development Surcharge — the margin between prescribed and sale price of gas.

nodes.label: Climate Support Levy
nodes.description: Climate Support Levy introduced during FY2025-26; budgeted at Rs 50 bn for FY2026-27.

nodes.label: Other Miscellaneous
nodes.description: Everything else: economic services, windfall levies, GIDC, LPG levy, off-grid captive power levy, UN receipts, attached-department receipts and foreign grants.

nodes.label: Borrowing & Other Financing
nodes.description: Because federal revenue does not cover federal spending, the gap (the federal deficit of Rs. 7,020 bn) is filled by borrowing and other financing: domestic bank and non-bank borrowing, net external loans, and privatisation proceeds.

nodes.label: Non-Bank Borrowing
nodes.description: Borrowing from non-bank sources — National Savings Schemes, GP Fund and public-account deposits.

nodes.label: Net External Receipts
nodes.description: Net loans from external sources — multilateral and bilateral lenders plus commercial loans and bonds.

nodes.label: Bank Borrowing
nodes.description: Domestic borrowing from banks through Treasury Bills, Pakistan Investment Bonds (PIBs) and Sukuk. This is the largest single financing item.

nodes.label: Privatisation Proceeds
nodes.description: Proceeds expected from the sale of state-owned assets.

nodes.label: Gross Revenue
nodes.description: Total federal revenue before the constitutionally-mandated transfer to the provinces: FBR taxes plus non-tax revenue (Rs. 20,600 bn).

nodes.label: Net Federal Revenue
nodes.description: What the federal government keeps after transferring the provinces' share of the divisible pool: gross revenue (Rs. 20,600 bn) minus the provincial transfer (Rs. 8,848 bn).

nodes.label: Transfer to Provinces (NFC)
nodes.description: Under Article 160 of the Constitution and the NFC Award, a fixed share (about 57.5%) of the divisible pool of federal taxes is transferred to the four provinces. At Rs. 8,848 bn this is larger than any single federal spending category — the federal government collects this money but never spends it itself.

facts.title: NFC distribution formula (among provinces)
facts.note: Under the 7th NFC Award (President’s Order 5 of 2010, as amended), provinces receive 57.5% of the net divisible pool. 1% of the pool goes to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa first for the war on terror; the remainder is distributed by this multi-indicator formula:

facts.title: Official province shares of the divisible pool
facts.note: Balochistan is guaranteed its projected amount; any shortfall is made up by the federal government.

nodes.label: Punjab
nodes.description: Punjab's share of the divisible pool (about 51.7% of the provincial share, based on the NFC's population-weighted formula).

nodes.label: Sindh
nodes.description: Sindh's share of the divisible pool (about 24.6% of the provincial share).

nodes.label: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
nodes.description: KP's share (about 14.6%), inclusive of the additional 1% of the divisible pool assigned for the war on terror.

nodes.label: Balochistan
nodes.description: Balochistan's share (about 9.1%). The federation guarantees Balochistan a projected minimum amount and makes up any shortfall from its own resources.

nodes.label: Total Federal Resources
nodes.description: The total pool of money the federal government has to spend: net federal revenue (Rs. 11,751 bn) plus borrowing and other financing (Rs. 7,020 bn). This equals total federal expenditure of Rs. 18,771 bn — the budget balances by design.

nodes.label: Current Expenditure
nodes.description: Day-to-day running costs of the federal government — 93% of all federal spending. Dominated by interest payments on debt, defence, pensions, grants and subsidies.

altBreakdowns.note: Current-expenditure demands for grants (charged + voted) from the demand-wise schedule — the parliamentary view of who is allocated money. Debt and loan repayments are excluded (refinancing, not expenditure). Classification differs slightly from the object-wise breakdown above.

altBreakdowns.note: The same Rs 17,495 bn classified by government function instead of by object, from the Annual Budget Statement.

items.label: General Public Service (incl. debt servicing & transfers)

nodes.label: Interest Payments
nodes.description: Mark-up (interest) on government debt — the single largest expense in the budget, larger than defence and development combined. Most of it services domestic debt.

nodes.label: Domestic Debt Interest
nodes.description: Interest paid on debt owed within Pakistan (T-Bills, PIBs, Sukuk, National Savings).

nodes.label: Foreign Debt Interest
nodes.description: Interest paid on external (foreign-currency) debt.

nodes.label: Pension
nodes.description: Pension payments to retired federal government employees, mostly military.

nodes.label: Military Pensions
nodes.description: Pensions for retired armed-forces personnel.

nodes.label: Civil Pensions
nodes.description: Pensions for retired civil government employees.

nodes.label: Pension Increase (Civil + Defence)
nodes.description: Provision for the budgeted increase in pension rates across civil and defence pensioners.

nodes.label: Federal Pension Fund
nodes.description: Contribution to the Federal Pension Fund set up to pre-fund future pension liabilities.

nodes.label: Defence Affairs & Services
nodes.description: The defence services budget (excludes military pensions, which are counted under Pension). The second-largest current expenditure after interest payments.

nodes.label: Grants & Transfers
nodes.description: Grants to provinces and other bodies, and social transfers. The largest single item is the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP).

nodes.label: Benazir Income Support Programme
nodes.description: BISP — Pakistan's flagship cash-transfer / social-protection programme for the poorest households.

nodes.label: Contingent Liabilities
nodes.description: Provision for government guarantees and contingent liabilities that may fall due.

nodes.label: Grants to Provinces
nodes.description: Discretionary grants to provinces (over and above the NFC divisible-pool transfer) — e.g. Sindh OZT and KP merged-districts support.

nodes.label: AJK Government
nodes.description: Grant to the Government of Azad Jammu & Kashmir.

nodes.label: Gilgit-Baltistan Government
nodes.description: Grant to the Government of Gilgit-Baltistan.

nodes.label: Pakistan Railways
nodes.description: Operating grant to Pakistan Railways.

nodes.label: Higher Education Commission
nodes.description: Recurrent grant to the Higher Education Commission (universities).

nodes.label: Other Grants & Transfers
nodes.description: All remaining grants and transfers grouped together — AJK/GB subventions aside, this includes provision for relief, Bait-ul-Mal, EPI, insurance schemes and many smaller bodies.

nodes.label: Miscellaneous Expenditure
nodes.description: Miscellaneous grant expenditure not classified elsewhere.

nodes.label: Security Enhancement
nodes.description: Grant for security enhancement measures.

nodes.label: Subsidies
nodes.description: Subsidies that keep prices below cost — overwhelmingly to the power sector.

nodes.label: Power Sector
nodes.description: Subsidies to the electricity sector (WAPDA/PEPCO, K-Electric, inter-DISCO tariff differential, AJK, merged districts, etc.) — the bulk of all subsidies.

nodes.label: Other Subsidies
nodes.description: Wheat subsidy to Gilgit-Baltistan, urea import subsidy, mark-up subsidies on housing and lending schemes, and other miscellaneous subsidies.

nodes.label: Industries & Production
nodes.description: Subsidies to industry — urea fertiliser production, the electric-vehicle incentive scheme, and Utility Stores arrears.

nodes.label: Food (PASSCO)
nodes.description: Subsidy to PASSCO for wheat reserve stock and the cost differential on wheat sales.

nodes.label: Running of Civil Govt.
nodes.description: The cost of running federal ministries, divisions and attached departments — salaries and operating costs of the civil government.

nodes.label: Emergency & Others
nodes.description: Provision for emergencies and other unallocated needs, including Rs. 20 bn earmarked for natural disasters.

source.table: Table 10 (vii) — Provision for Emergency and others

nodes.label: Development & Net Lending
nodes.description: Money spent building things and lending onward — the Federal Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) plus net lending. Just 7% of federal spending.

nodes.label: Federal PSDP
nodes.description: The Federal Public Sector Development Programme — the federal government's development / infrastructure budget, spread across ministries, corporations and special areas.

nodes.label: National Highway Authority
nodes.description: Roads and highways built by the NHA — the largest single PSDP allocation.

nodes.label: Water Resources
nodes.description: Dams, irrigation and water-storage projects under the Water Resources Division.

nodes.label: Special Areas (AJK & GB)
nodes.description: Development projects in Azad Jammu & Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.

nodes.label: Provincial Projects
nodes.description: Federally-funded development projects located in the provinces.

nodes.label: Power Division (NTDC/PEPCO)
nodes.description: Power transmission and generation development projects.

nodes.label: Cabinet Division
nodes.description: Development projects run under the Cabinet Division.

nodes.label: Merged Districts of KP
nodes.description: Development spending in the former FATA (merged districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa).

nodes.label: Higher Education Commission
nodes.description: Development / infrastructure grants to universities via the HEC.

nodes.label: Railways Division
nodes.description: Development projects for Pakistan Railways.

nodes.label: Federal Education & Training
nodes.description: Federal Education & Professional Training Division development projects.

nodes.label: Other PSDP
nodes.description: All remaining PSDP allocations grouped together — dozens of smaller ministries and divisions, plus SOEs, project liabilities and CPEC 2.0 new initiatives.

nodes.label: Net Lending
nodes.description: Loans the federal government extends (net of recoveries), mainly to public-sector entities and provinces.
